reviews.one_line_contribution: A substrate-swap test asking whether the dose-dependent harm of in-context retrieved agent experience survives being moved into LoRA weights by context distillation: a student distilled from a harmful k=7 teacher is predicted to be equivalent to one distilled from a benign k=3 teacher, which would locate memory harm on the read path (query-item interference) rather than in a transferable behavioral disposition.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two distinct threats, both verified with the literature CLI. (1) For P1: arXiv:2607.21051 'Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience' (verified, 2026-07-23) already establishes that context distillation of agent interaction histories preserves most in-context gains at far lower sample cost, with direct SFT far weaker; the proposal concedes this, which means the first of its two confirmatory claims is a cost-normalized replication. (2) For P2, the actual mechanism claim, the closest work is the 'privilege illusion' family in on-policy/privileged distillation: DAPD (arXiv:2608.01735, verified via s2) and DOPD (arXiv:2606.30626) both characterize students trained from a privileged-context teacher acquiring context-dependent behavior they cannot reproduce without the context, and arXiv:2608.05219 (When Privileged Guidance Misaligns) and arXiv:2607.05184 study exactly which teacher-context-induced behaviors fail to transfer to a student that lacks the context. This does not collide outright — none of them uses a *harmful* context as the probe, none measures a one-sided break signature, none is on retrieved agent experience memory — but it means the proposal's central mechanism (behavior conditioned on a context block does not survive removal of that block) is a documented phenomenon under another name, so P2's confirming outcome is close to the expected one. Cutting the other way, and unaddressed by the proposal: arXiv:2507.14805 (Subliminal Learning, verified in search) and arXiv:2606.22019 (Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning) show behavioral traits do transmit through distillation even on semantically unrelated data, and arXiv:2505.24842 (Cascading Adversarial Bias from Injection to Distillation) shows bias injected into a teacher's context propagates and amplifies in students. A reviewer will ask why the proposal cites none of this, since it is the literature that makes P2 non-trivial and supplies its positive-control design.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory test cannot distinguish its two hypotheses, because the equivalence margin is larger than the effect it is about. The harm being probed is the pilot's 'broke six to seven items, fixed none'; on the proposed 465-task held-out set that is roughly 1.3 points, and Gate 0 only requires that break-minus-fix be significantly positive by McNemar, which a 1-2 point effect can be. P2 then declares the asymmetry established if P-CDh minus P-CD3 falls inside +/-3 points by TOST, against a stated minimum detectable paired difference of 3-4 points. So P2 is satisfied even if one hundred percent of the harm distilled: 'harm does not distill' and 'harm distills but is invisible at this resolution' are not separated by the design as written. The second half of P2, that P-CDh's broken-minus-fixed count is 'not significantly positive', is a failure-to-reject presented as evidence for a null, which the proposal's own Measurement section explicitly forbids ('every predicted null is tested as equivalence with a stated margin, never as a failure to reject'). Compounding this, the design has no positive control: nothing in the plan demonstrates that a genuinely dispositional harm would be detected by this pipeline if it were present, so a null is uninformative rather than substrate-level evidence. And the null is close to foregone in any case — the program's own starting position already reports that injection volume, not memory content, was the causal lever (7 items harmful, 3 items benign, same bank), i.e. the harm was already measured to be a load effect on the read path; removing the block at student inference removes the load by construction. The proposal even schedules a decoy arm designed to reconfirm load-drivenness. Finally, the whole novel half is contingent on Gate 0 firing on Qwen2.5-7B, and the stated fallback ('reports retained value and cost only') is precisely the replication of 2607.21051 that the authors agree is not a contribution.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three changes. (1) Tie the equivalence margin to the measured effect rather than fixing it at 3 points: pre-register margin = one half of the in-context k_h harm measured at Gate 0, and make Gate 0 pass only if the k_h harm is large enough (on this sample, roughly 6+ points paired) that an equivalence test at that margin has the stated 80 percent power; if the harm is smaller, the asymmetry claim is untestable and should be declared so up front rather than 'confirmed' by an underpowered TOST. Test the break-signature half of P2 as an equivalence on the discordant-pair rate, not as a non-significant McNemar. (2) Add a positive control that closes the inferential gap: construct a teacher context that is known to induce a dispositional bias rather than load interference — the program already has candidates in its own appendix (majority-action prior, memory-induced shortcutting) — distill from it under the identical pipeline, and show the pipeline detects transfer. Without a demonstrated sensitivity to dispositional transfer, the headline null carries no weight. (3) Add the k=0 teacher arm described under missing_baseline, and cite and engage the subliminal-learning and injected-bias-propagation results (2507.14805, 2606.22019, 2505.24842) and the privilege-illusion family (2608.01735, 2606.30626, 2608.05219), which are the literature that makes the question live. Trimming the ablation list (rank sweep, KL-vs-CE, temperature, half steps) would buy the compute for the positive control and the extra seeds, and would fix the feasibility problem at the same time.
reviews.missing_baseline: P-CD0: context distillation from a teacher run with an empty retrieval block (k=0) on the same train tasks, i.e. plain self-distillation on the base model's own on-distribution ALFWorld generations. Every parametric arm in the plan trains on freshly generated teacher outputs, while the only non-retrieval reference (P-SFT) trains on raw pooled trajectories — so the P-CD3-minus-P-SFT gap the plan reads as 'retained in-context value' is confounded with the generation format and on-policy-ness of teacher outputs versus raw pool text. Self-training on ALFWorld train tasks alone is a large known effect, and without P-CD0 the retained-value fraction in P1 cannot be attributed to the retrieved experience at all. A reviewer will also want the P-CDh success-filtered arm matched to P-CD3 on training-token count and on teacher success rate, since the k_h teacher is by construction the weaker generator and any P-CDh deficit has a mundane data-quality explanation that the plan does not separate from 'harm distilled'.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. Channel (a), the project CLI (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers), answered every query; WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so no query used channel (b). Queries run: Q1 'context distillation of retrieved agent experience into weights does harm transfer' (--recent) returned 2609.02749, 2608.26730, 2608.12307, 2607.21051, 2607.10608, 2512.02543, 2506.14728, 2501.19400 — none distills from a harmful dose. Q2 'does distillation inherit negative transfer from harmful in-context demonstrations student teacher' returned 2608.16647, 2606.30626, 2606.22019, 2605.30833, 2605.23857, 2512.20908, 2507.14805, 2502.02671 — the subliminal-learning line here is the closest thing to a contradicting result and is absent from the proposal. Q3 'Experience Distillation internalize agent interaction histories into weights retains in-context gains' (closest named method) returned 2607.21051, 2607.28272, 2606.24428, 2606.04703, 2602.12275, 2209.15189. Q4 'same experience pool in context versus in weights matched compute retained value agent memory' returned 2607.28272, 2607.10608, 2606.24775, 2605.18421, 2605.12493, 2602.16313 — no matched-pool substrate comparison. Q5 'distilling from a degraded or noisy context teacher student does not inherit context interference' (--recent) returned nothing on point (2609.01532, 2606.11173, 2605.30833, 2606.00105). Q6 'privilege illusion student cannot reproduce privileged context behavior distillation agents' (--recent) returned 2608.01735, 2606.30626, 2608.05219, 2607.05184, 2608.25936, 2602.04942 — the nearest mechanism neighbours. Q7 'number of retrieved in-context examples dose response harm agent trajectories retrieval load interference' (--recent) returned 2606.22338 (RoboMME-Interference: memory degrades under long-context interference unless retrieval isolates relevant demonstrations, adjacent to the load account), 2607.19257, 2607.10608. ID verification: I verified 2607.21051, 2607.01480 (PMD), 2606.04703, 2606.02355 (SIRI), 2605.27762 (PEAM), 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap), 2608.10775 (SkillLens/CardDistill), 2606.29961 (DuoMem), 2608.07169 (Agent Memory Distillation), 2601.03192 (MemRL) and 2607.28272 (MemHarness) with s2cli paper; all resolve and match the proposal's descriptions, including 2606.04703's off-policy-is-more-stable finding. I confirmed 2602.12275, 2512.02543, 2506.14728, 2501.19400, 2507.14805, 2505.24842, 2606.22019, 2608.01735 and 2608.05219 through search results. I could NOT verify 2603.18272 (the claimed Qwen2.5-7B precedent), 2605.28889, 2608.02508, 2608.15008, 2603.01097, 2606.03197, 2603.13017, 2607.29032, 2607.22629, 2606.29502, 2604.05112 or 2306.07929 — none of these carries the novelty argument, but the backbone-precedent ID is unchecked. Judgment of the check itself: it is above average for this pipeline — four queries, channels named, IDs listed, and an honest concession that P1 is a replication of 2607.21051 rather than a contribution. Its real weakness is scope, not effort: all four queries stay inside the agent-memory neighbourhood, and none searches the distillation-side literature where the mechanism claim actually lives, so it misses both the work that would have supported the claim's non-triviality (subliminal trait transfer, injected-bias cascade) and the work that already characterizes context-conditioned behavior failing to survive context removal (the privilege-illusion family). An unsearched neighbourhood that contains the closest mechanistic prior is a weakness in the novelty argument, not a neutral.
